purpose: Teach: つたの/見込ま/名づけ/転がっ/くっつい/とどまる/はじまる/かかえ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、垣根にはつたのからまる家が多かった
lines.en: You know, when I was young, there were so many houses with ivy climbing up their hedges.
lines.style: Soft, distant gaze into memory. Slow measured pace. Voice settles into the image like watching something recede. Gentle breathiness on the opening.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、お孫様の出世を見込まれてたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Mm-hmm. Your father was always so sure you'd go far, wasn't he, dear?
lines.style: Warm, affectionate. Reaches back to meet his memory with her own. Gentle lilt on "wasn't he" — not quite a question, more like settling a shared fact between them.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが孫を「ちびすけ」と名づけられた
lines.en: When I was young, my father used to call me "Little One" — that's what stuck with me.
lines.style: Voice grows quieter, more intimate. Pause before the nickname like he can hear it again. Tender around the edges, almost fragile with the weight of it.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、いつもお手玉が転がってたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you'd always have your beanbags scattered about on the veranda, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Gentle, knowing smile in the voice. Light rhythm like she's naming small, beloved habits. The "dear" lands with warmth, not formality.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんに孫がくっついて離れなかった
lines.en: When I was young, I used to follow my father everywhere — wouldn't let him out of my sight.
lines.style: Voice carries both the boy's devotion and the old man's recognition of it. Slight catch on "wouldn't let him" — the child's grip still present in memory.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、晩年は縁側にとどまる時間が長かったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: In his later years, he'd spend such long hours just sitting on the veranda, wouldn't he, dear?
lines.style: Softer now, knowing. Pace slows slightly — matching the quiet of those hours. "Dear" lands like a hand on his arm, gentle acknowledgment of what they both understand.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お祭りがはじまると村中が湧いた
lines.en: When I was young, the whole village would come alive the moment the festival started.
lines.style: Voice brightens slightly — a memory of excitement and gathering. Pace quickens just enough to catch the energy of it. Opens wide on "festival," like the sound carries the commotion.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、米俵をかかえて運ばれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And there you were, carrying sacks of rice on your shoulders, weren't you, dear?
lines.style: Warmth with a hint of admiration. Voice settles comfortably, like she can see him doing it. The "dear" is intimate now — she's looking at him across all these years, still seeing that young man.
